lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: June 2026. A three-week-old calf in Zavala County, Texas, is found with maggots in its navel.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: Not ordinary maggots. These eat living flesh.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: The New World screwworm. America wiped it out in 1966. Now it's back.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: And the weapon that beat it last time wasn't a poison. It was more flies. Billions of them.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: Here's how it works. A female lays two hundred fifty to five hundred eggs at the edge of a wound, or a newborn's navel.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: The maggots burrow into healthy flesh. Disturb them, and they screw in deeper. That's the name.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: The wound draws more flies. Left alone, it can kill the animal.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: Cattle, deer, dogs, cats. Even, sometimes, people.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: In good years, it spread all the way to the Canadian border.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: In the nineteen thirties, two government scientists, Edward Knipling and Raymond Bushland, went looking for a better way to fight it.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: And they found a weakness. A female screwworm mates only once in her life.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: So what if her one mate was sterile? Flood the land with sterile males, and wild females lay eggs that never hatch.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: But how do you sterilize a fly? The clue came from a book by Nobel laureate Hermann Muller, on radiation and genes.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: Bushland borrowed an army X-ray machine in Kerrville, Texas. In six months, he had the dose.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: They published in 1951.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: A first test on Sanibel Island, Florida, backed the idea. But Sanibel sits right off the coast. They wanted proof.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: So, in 1954, they went to Curaçao, an island in the Caribbean. Every week, an airplane dropped sterile flies over it.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: After three weeks, about seventy percent of the egg masses they found were sterile. Within about two months, fertile eggs were gone.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: In 1955, the results and the theory went to print, side by side.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: Then they scaled up. Florida first, in 1958. Then the whole Southwest.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: By 1966, the screwworm was gone from the United States. Over the next decade, America and Mexico released more than ninety four billion sterile flies.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: Mexico was declared free in 1991. Then, country by country, Central America.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: Today, a plant in Panama releases up to a hundred million sterile flies a week, a living wall at the Darién Gap.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: Even when it slipped into the Florida Keys in 2016, attacking endangered Key deer, it was beaten by March 2017.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: Then, in late 2024, the wall broke. Screwworms showed up in southern Mexico, and started moving north.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: In July 2025, the US closed the border to Mexican cattle.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: The fly kept coming. Seventy miles from the border. Then thirty one.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: Then, June third, 2026. Texas.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: By the end of October, seventy one cases. Texas, New Mexico, Arizona. Cattle, and dogs, and a cat.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: So America is doing what worked before. Sterile flies are dropping over Texas again.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: And a new fly factory at Moore Air Base in Edinburg, Texas, is meant to start by the end of this year. A hundred million flies at first. Three hundred million by 2028.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: If you have animals, check their wounds. Report maggots to a vet or the USDA. And no, your beef is safe.

lines.speaker: nar
lines.text: We beat this fly once, not with poison, but with one strange fact. She only mates once. Now, we have to do it again.
